findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Deleting on Err is justified as covering a close, but an Err does not close the job
findings.evidence: run/close.rs:170-175: hold_for_disk returns an Err, and the job 'stays dispatched' until 'the next drain resumes the job from its kept candidate (Athena::retry)'. So an Err from the run does not close the job. Decision 2 nonetheless counts 'error' as a close outcome. Fix: Say why deleting on Err is correct: a resumed job runs under its own job id and pushes its own athena/ci/<id>, so the held job's branch would otherwise be left behind. Also add to the open questions that a process killed outright (no Err) leaves athena/ci/<old id> on the remote, and nothing in this job removes it.

findings.summary: test_support.rs is needed but not listed
findings.evidence: EarlyFake is defined at test_support.rs:260 and implements Remote at :309. Without routing by branch, the CI pushes would change existing run_pin_tests assertions such as fail_push at run_pin_tests.rs:516 and :550. Athena already flagged that the file is not listed. Fix: Keep the change, but list test_support.rs as a required deliverable and explain why (EarlyFake is the shared fake behind early_seam), so the producer is not stopped by the file list.

findings.summary: The default delete_branch assertion only shows that something exists
findings.evidence: The assertion that the test FakeRemote's default delete_branch returns an error only shows that a default exists. It does not demonstrate any requested behavior. Fix: Drop that assertion, or keep it only as a guard. The real-git delete test is the evidence that matters.

findings.summary: Hard-coded probe counts depend on whether planning runs
findings.evidence: The probe counts agents run so far. If the ci_run helper's setup turns on planning, planner and critic runs would change the expected values. Fix: Have ci_run turn planning off explicitly, or work out the expected probe from the counts the helper sets up rather than hard-coding 1 and 2.

summary: I read gh/early.rs (early_pr, early_pr_to, https_github_repository), run/mod.rs (dispatch at lines 924-949 and check_and_verify at 1174-1201), run/close.rs (hold_for_disk), and the EarlyFake and early_seam names in test_support.rs and gh/mod.rs. Every function and seam the plan names exists where it says. The push goes next to early_pr, after admission and the disk gate, and uses the same origin check and the same cfg(test) seam lookup, so a test with a github.com origin cannot reach the network. The finish_dispatched wrapper covers the two paths that can push, the resume path and the produce_and_verify path. The demonstrations drive Athena::go with a recording EarlyFake and would fail without the behavior: no CI push, no delete, and a skip-line count of 0 or 2 all fail them. A real-git test covers GitRemote::delete_branch. The design is sound: probing the remote before acting (remote_head) avoids false warnings, and replace pinned to the old head deals with leftover branches. Nothing below is a blocker or major. The minor points: test_support.rs is outside the listed files (Athena already flagged this; the reason given is valid). The plan says deleting on Err is about covering outcomes, but the real reason is that held or interrupted jobs are resumed under a new job id, and the plan should say so. One gh/tests.rs assertion only shows that a default exists.
